svg.title: Five gates between a change in Dataverse and a flow run
svg.desc: A funnel from all activity changes to the useful work, with illustrative numbers. Gate 1, change type and table: Added or Modified on Phone Calls. Gate 2, scope: Organization, rows of any owner. Gate 3, Select columns, for updates only: statecode must be included in the update request; included does not mean changed; lookup columns are not supported. Gate 4, Filter rows: statecode eq 1 and directioncode eq true and the regarding value is not null must be true for the row after the save; this tests the state of the row, not the transition. These four gates are evaluated by Dataverse from the callback registration; changes that fail never reach Power Automate. Gate 5, trigger condition, evaluated by Power Automate on the trigger data: the regarding type equals incidents; if false, no run is created and nothing appears in the run history. After the gates a run exists, and a Condition action inside it checks what only the case knows: active and not yet marked. Illustrative day: 6,000 activity changes, 140 reach Power Automate, 55 runs start, 38 cases are updated.
svg.text: Five gates before a run exists (numbers are illustrative for one day)
Evaluated by DATAVERSE (callback registration) — nothing is sent for changes that fail
Organization: rows of any owner (relative to the flow owner)
statecode must be INCLUDED in the update request
included ≠ changed · no lookups · no primary key
Gate 4 · Filter rows (OData, after the save)
statecode eq 1 and directioncode eq true
and _regardingobjectid_value ne null — state, not transition
Evaluated by POWER AUTOMATE — false = no run, nothing in the run history
Get the case → Condition: active and not yet
↓ most updates do not include statecode
